authority_scope: source-neutral restricted identifier and hash scanning
content A and optional metadata B relationships

pack_local_tooling_grant.scope: A pack owner may create one pack-local source-neutral scan authority, scanner, process-receipt schema, receipt generator, and validator in a tooling-foundation commit made before candidate-affecting work. The tools and inputs must satisfy this authority exactly and must be hash-bound by every resulting receipt.
prohibited: source-specific names, identifiers, paths, or assets
private oracle values or hidden cases
post-hoc claims about an authoring process that was not contemporaneously recorded
hard-coded PASS values without executed commands and result evidence

restricted_identifier_and_hash_scan.proof_limit: This scan detects generic evidence leakage, foreign namespaces, unclassified hashes, and prohibited production paths. Source-specific semantic or identifier comparison remains private T10 work after candidate freeze.

hash_policy.scan: Every lowercase 64-hex token in tracked candidate text objects.
classified_when: the token equals a SHA-256 of an exact blob reachable from content A or metadata B

the token equals a SHA-256 of a committed producer-safe assignment, contract, launch packet, allocation, schema, scanner, validator, receipt, test result, or package artifact explicitly listed by the candidate manifest

input_scope: all paths and blobs reachable from content A
all paths and blobs introduced by optional metadata B
BP, RP, MCAddon, editable asset sources, tests, tools, reports, receipts, and manifests
restricted_identifier_and_hash_scan.pass_semantics: PASS only when every required input is scanned, matches is empty, foreign_namespaces is empty, unclassified_hashes is empty, and the scanner exits zero.
restricted_identifier_and_hash_scan.failure_semantics: Any missing input, unreadable blob, invalid authority, scanner exception, nonzero exit, match, foreign namespace, or unclassified hash is FAIL.

filesystem_checks: Git object files have link count one.
The Git object store resolves inside the assigned repository.
No alternates file or configured alternate exists.
Every object in the object database is reachable from an owned authority ref.
Content A descends from the allocated baseline.
Metadata B descends from content A when present.
restricted_git_object_scan.pass_semantics: PASS only when Git fsck succeeds, all required commands execute, no prohibited repository linkage exists, every object is owned and reachable, and required ancestry holds.
restricted_git_object_scan.failure_semantics: A missing command, ambiguous Git directory, remote, alternate, hardlink, escaping symlink, unreachable object, fsck error, or ancestry failure is FAIL.

candidate_bound_process_receipt.candidate_binding: The receipt must bind the process that authored content A. It must not be generated retroactively by a later process.
cleanup_semantics: temporary home and cache disposition recorded
temporary files and logs either removed or committed as declared evidence
no unexpected mount or remote remains
candidate_bound_process_receipt.pass_semantics: PASS requires contemporaneous process identity, exact sanitized inputs, executed denial probes, executed scans, exact output hashes, successful cleanup, and explicit cooperative-boundary proof limits.
candidate_bound_process_receipt.failure_semantics: Missing contemporaneous process evidence, retroactive reconstruction, an unbound tool/input, a failed or absent denial probe, an absent scan, cleanup ambiguity, or candidate mismatch is FAIL.

execution_order: Commit tooling foundation containing schema and validator.
Launch the candidate-affecting authoring process with the committed tooling and sanitized inputs.
Freeze content A and exact package artifacts.
After the authoring process exits, generate the candidate-bound process receipt.
Run the precommitted validator from a separate process after the receipt exists.
Commit the receipt and validation result in metadata B.
T1 reruns the exact hash-bound validator during mechanical preflight.
independent_noncircular_receipt_validati.pass_semantics: PASS only when the receipt already exists, the validator and schema match their pre-authoring commit hashes, validation runs in a separate process, findings is empty, and exit status is zero.
independent_noncircular_receipt_validati.failure_semantics: Self-declared receipt validity, validation before receipt creation, validator mutation after authoring, missing hashes, any finding, or nonzero exit is FAIL.

candidate_message_mechanics.generation_zero: Internal preliminary build only; never a candidate submission.
candidate_message_mechanics.replacement_generation: Increment by exactly one for every replacement publication, including metadata-only or envelope-only corrections.
candidate_message_mechanics.parent_message_id: null for the first submission; exact repair, rejection, or prior candidate message for a replacement.

idempotency_derivation.canonical_encoding: UTF-8 JSON with keys sorted lexicographically, separators comma and colon, ensure_ascii true, and no trailing newline

content_a.production_commit: Exact immutable content commit containing implementation and package artifacts.
content_a.artifact_paths: Repository-relative POSIX paths tracked in production_commit; absolute paths, dot segments, traversal, symlinks, and untracked files are forbidden.

metadata_b.metadata_commit: Exact descendant commit containing only allowlisted evidence and candidate metadata.
metadata_b.metadata_parent_commit: The first parent of metadata B must equal content A exactly.
metadata_b.metadata_changed_paths: Explicit sorted list; every path must be evidence, receipt, report, or candidate metadata and must not alter BP, RP, editable assets, runtime, tests, builder, or package bytes.
metadata_b.evidence_paths: Repository-relative POSIX paths tracked in metadata_commit with exact size and SHA-256.

candidate_message_mechanics.source_authority_semantics: source_authority_commit/tree bind metadata B when present, otherwise content A. production_commit/tree always bind content A.
candidate_message_mechanics.artifact_manifest_semantics: The top-level artifact_manifest object must bind its repository, ref, commit, tree, relative path, size, and SHA-256. Every BP/RP/MCAddon entry must do the same.
candidate_message_mechanics.tests_semantics: The top-level tests object must name executed suites, pass/fail counts, receipt paths and hashes, exact candidate binding, and any carried-forward evidence with an unchanged-package proof.

aperture_c0_disposition.reason: No contemporaneous candidate-bound authoring-process receipt or independent post-creation validation exists in C0. A later receipt cannot retroactively prove its authoring boundary.
aperture_c0_disposition.preservation: C0, its Git authority, and exact package bytes remain immutable and may be used only as quarantined product-progress history, not as a promotable or test-routed candidate.

aperture_authorized_next_action.repository_initialization: The durable Aperture owner is authorized to initialize only this exact repository path as a fresh independent Git object store with no remotes, alternates, hardlinks, or shared worktree. This is not authority to alter or delete the preserved C0 repository.
initial_inputs: the existing producer-safe Aperture launch packet
prohibited_inputs: Aperture C0 repository or package bytes
Aperture C0 code, assets, tests, manifests, builders, reports, or identifiers
Java evidence, source artifacts, source names and paths, decompiled material, private oracle, or hidden cases
aperture_authorized_next_action.tooling_order: Create and commit the pack-local scanner, schemas, receipt generator, validator, and launch profile before any product-affecting write.
aperture_authorized_next_action.worker_model: The durable owner may spawn one fresh bounded producer that has not inspected C0. The parent may pass only the enumerated source-neutral inputs and may not translate C0 details into the prompt.
aperture_authorized_next_action.completion: Publish MSG-P12-APERTURE-CANDIDATE-000001 only after exact package freeze, contemporaneous process receipt, executed scans, noncircular validation, and local required gates pass.
